test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: ‘Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh’ was written by ______ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abdul Qadir Badauni.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book **"Muntakhab-al-Tawarikh"** was written by **Abd al-Qadir Badauni.**

 
 
• He began writing this history in the first half of **1590**.
 
• The book was completed in **October 1595**.
 
• It comprises the **618 solar year's** historic events.
 
• This book is based on Khawaja Nizam-ud-din Ahmad Sirhindi's Tabaqat-i-Akbar Shahi.
 
 
 
• This work in three volumes is a general history of the Muslims of India:
 
 
• The first contains the rulers and kings of **Ghaznavids, Ghurid dynasty, Mamluk Dynasty, Babur, and Humayun**.
 
• Second, covers the first 40 years of Mughal Emperor Akbar's reign from **14 February 1556 to October 1595.**
 
• The third contains biographical accounts of the Saints, Poets who were attached to the court of Akbar.
 
 
 
• The accounts relate to **38 Shaykhs, 69 scholars, 15 philosophers, physicians, and 67 poets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Akbar (1556-1605)**

 
• Akbar was one of the greatest monarchs of the **Mughal dynasty**.
 
• He was the son of **Humayun and Hamida Banu Begum, born at Amarkot in c. 1542 CE.**
 
• He was crowned at Kalanaur in c. 1556 CE at the young age of 13 years and 4 months.
 
• Akbar's biography is **Akabarnama** written by **Abul Fazal**.
 
• The Akbar Nama is divided into **three** books: The first book dealt with **Akbar's ancestors**. The second recorded the events of **Akbar's reign**. The third is the **Ain-i Akbari**.

**Dara Shikoh (1615-1659)**

 
• He was the eldest son of **Shah Jahan**. He is described as a **“liberal Muslim”** who tried to find commonalities between Hindu and Islamic traditions.
 
• He is known as a pioneer of the academic movement for interfaith understanding in India. He had a deep understanding and knowledge of major religions, particularly Islam and Hinduism.
 
• He was assassinated by Aurangzeb, in a bitter struggle for the throne on 30th August 1659 when he was 44.
 
• He translated the Upanishads and other important sources of Hindu religion and spirituality from Sanskrit to Persian. Through these translations, he was responsible for taking the Hindu culture and spiritual traditions to Europe and the West.

**Jahanara Begum Sahib (1614-1681)**

 
• She was the eldest daughter of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• Together with her brother Dara Shikoh, she was a disciple of Mullah Shah Badakhshi, who initiated her into the Qadiriyya Sufi order in 1641.
 
• Jahanara Begum made such progress on the Sufi path that Mullah Shah would have named her his successor in the Qadiriyya, but the rules of the order did not allow this.
 
• She wrote a biography of **Moinuddin Chishti**, the founder of the Chishtiyah order, titled "**Mu'nis al-Arwāḥ"**, as well as a biography of Mullah Shah, titled **Risalah-i Şāḥibiyah,** in which she also described her initiation by him.
